vulnerabilities.description: Next.js 14.2.35 contains multiple high-severity vulnerabilities: XSS in CSP nonces (GHSA-ffhc-5mcf-pf4q), cache poisoning (GHSA-vfv6-92ff-j949, GHSA-wfc6-r584-vfw7), DoS attacks (GHSA-q4gf-8mx6-v5v3, GHSA-h25m-26qc-wcjf), HTTP smuggling (GHSA-ggv3-7p47-pfv8), and SSRF (GHSA-c4j6-fc7j-m34r)
glob 10.2.0-10.4.5 vulnerable to command injection via -c/--cmd flag (GHSA-5j98-mcp5-4vw2). Executes matches with shell:true allowing arbitrary command execution
Next.js Image Optimizer DoS vulnerabilities (GHSA-9g9p-9gw9-jx7f) and unbounded disk cache growth (GHSA-3x4c-7xq6-9pq8)
Session and memory data stored as plaintext JSON at .claude-flow/data/memory.json without encryption
Session context stored in plaintext at .claude-flow/sessions/ directory without encryption
Only validates key format but not value content. Could allow injection of malicious JSON

recommendations: 1. UPDATE DEPENDENCIES IMMEDIATELY: Run 'npm audit fix --force' to update Next.js, glob, and PostCSS to patched versions
2. Upgrade Next.js from 14.2.35 to 16.2.6+ to fix 15+ security vulnerabilities
3. Update glob to 10.5.0+ to patch command injection vulnerability
4. Update PostCSS to 8.5.10+ to fix XSS vulnerability
5. Implement encryption for .claude-flow/data/memory.json using crypto module
6. Add schema validation in memory.js for stored values
7. Enable Content Security Policy (CSP) headers in deployment
8. Monitor Google AdSense/Analytics property IDs for unauthorized use
9. No hardcoded secrets found - maintain current practice of using NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix for exposed env vars
10. Document that user favorites/history are stored client-side in localStorage and can be cleared
